reconcile.note: Gill reads 1 Samuel 21:1's "alone" as alone before the priest only, since David's servants waited elsewhere and later shared the showbread.

discrepancy.note: Troki argues David came to Ahimelech alone, not with followers as Mark's Gospel account implies.

quotes.text: Nor did David come to Ahimelech with his followers, as the above quotation from Mark would lead one to suppose. For Ahimelech asked David (1 Samuel xxi. 1), "Why art thou alone, and no man with thee?"
quotes.attr: Isaac ben Abraham Troki (d. 1594), Faith Strengthened (Chizzuk Emunah), Part 2, ch. 28 (1851 trans.), on 1 Samuel 21:1.

sides.snippet: Why are you alone, and no man with you?
sides.verseText: Then came David to Nob to Ahimelech the priest: and Ahimelech came to meet David trembling, and said to him, Why are you alone, and no man with you?

sides.snippet: how he entered into the house of God, and ate the show bread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for those who were with him
sides.verseText: how he entered into the house of God, and ate the show bread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for those who were with him, but only for the priests?
